lead.headline: Tata Motors CV swings to profit and calls Iveco bid final; CG Power orders jump 90%, Tonbo lists 66% up
lead.dek: Tata Motors' commercial-vehicle business returned to profit on 36% revenue growth and said its €14.40 Iveco offer will not be raised, with tenders at 35% against an 80% threshold. CG Power's order intake nearly doubled, defence-electronics maker Tonbo Imaging listed at a 66% premium, and MoRTH proposed making emergency braking mandatory on cars, while commodity inflation cut JK Tyre's margin almost in half.

ev.headline: Ultraviolette plans ₹800 crore Hosur plant and new 100V platform as it targets exports
ev.summary: Bengaluru-based electric motorcycle maker Ultraviolette plans a facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, with capacity of 2.5 lakh units and an investment of about ₹800 crore, including battery production lines, alongside its existing 50,000-unit plant near Bengaluru. It launched the VX-100 100V platform with the X-47 Venom at an introductory ₹2.65 lakh for the first 5,000 buyers, and plans four more launches over the next year. The company targets exports of 20–25% of sales within two to three years and aims for about 20,000 vehicles a month within two years.
ev.whyItMatters: A capacity build-out of this size at a privately held premium e-2W maker points to a sizeable funding requirement, making it a likely candidate for growth equity or eventual ECM activity.

ev.headline: Tsuyo ties up with China's LvKON to make electric CV powertrains in India
ev.summary: Tsuyo Manufacturing has signed a technical partnership with Suzhou Lvkon Transmission (LvKON), a Chinese electric drive-system supplier it has worked with for five years, to produce electric drive systems for trucks, buses and off-road vehicles in India. Tsuyo is also progressing plans for a 24-acre greenfield campus covering e-powertrain engineering, assembly, testing and application development.
ev.whyItMatters: Technology tie-ups with Chinese suppliers are becoming the quickest route to localising e-CV drivetrains, and could grow into JV or minority-stake structures as truck and bus electrification picks up.

ev.headline: Shakti Pumps puts another ₹12 crore into its EV-components subsidiary, taking total to ₹92 crore
ev.summary: Shakti Pumps has invested a further ₹12 crore in its wholly owned subsidiary Shakti EV Mobility through 1.2 crore equity shares, bringing its total investment to ₹92 crore. The unit makes EV motors, chargers and controllers, and its turnover rose to ₹24.25 crore in FY26 from ₹3.73 crore in FY25.
ev.whyItMatters: Diversified industrials are incubating EV-component businesses inside listed parents, which could later lead to carve-outs or strategic stake sales once these units reach scale.

autos.headline: Tata Motors CV posts ₹1,257 crore Q2 profit on 36% revenue growth; calls Iveco offer final
autos.summary: Tata Motors, the demerged commercial-vehicle company, reported Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹1,257 crore against a ₹867 crore loss a year earlier, with revenue up 36.3% to ₹25,338 crore and a net cash position of ₹15,900 crore. Wholesales rose 42% to about 1.35 lakh units, with exports up 177%, although management said commodity inflation hurt operating margins by about 540 bps YoY. It described its €14.40-a-share Iveco offer as 'best and final', with tenders at 35% against the 80% needed and settlement planned for 30 October.
autos.whyItMatters: The coming week decides India's largest outbound auto acquisition; whether the 80% threshold is met will determine the Dutch squeeze-out route, the financing structure and when Iveco is consolidated.

autos.headline: JK Tyre's Q2 profit falls 73% as raw-material costs halve its margin; plans 4–5% Q3 price rise
autos.summary: JK Tyre & Industries' Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.7% to ₹4,840.73 crore, with domestic sales up 32% (OEM up 65%), but net profit fell 73% to ₹59.99 crore. EBITDA fell 35.9% to ₹343.14 crore and margin narrowed to 7.1% from 13.4%, as the raw-material basket rose about 30% over six months. After 11–12% of price increases in H1, the company plans a further 4–5% in Q3.
autos.whyItMatters: Margin compression across tyre makers (CEAT reported a similar squeeze last week) is resetting FY27 earnings estimates for the segment and is a key valuation input for any auto-ancillary transactions.

autos.headline: Bosch to carve its German Mobility business into a separate subsidiary from August 2027
autos.summary: Bosch plans to move its German Mobility business and three central service units into four wholly owned subsidiaries from 1 August 2027, transferring about 62,500 Germany-based employees. Mobility generated €55.8 bn of sales in 2025 and €27.8 bn in H1 2026, while its operating margin reportedly fell to 1.8% from 3.8%. Bosch has ruled out an IPO, a sale or a merger of the unit, citing competition, especially from Asia.
autos.whyItMatters: The world's largest auto supplier ring-fencing its mobility arm signals deeper restructuring among European tier-1s, which could free up non-core assets and push more engineering and sourcing toward lower-cost bases such as India.

industrials.headline: CG Power Q2 profit up 44% to ₹409 crore; order intake rises 90% to ₹8,016 crore
industrials.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions reported Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹409.09 crore, up 44% from ₹284.44 crore, as revenue rose 30.1% to ₹3,802 crore. EBITDA rose 43.1% to ₹539.6 crore, with margin up 130 bps to 14.2%, and order intake rose 90% YoY to ₹8,016 crore. The board approved new capex, including a 10,000 MVA power-transformer expansion and a ₹300 crore bushings and instrument-transformer plant at Ambad.
industrials.whyItMatters: Strong order inflows and margin gains at a leading transformer and switchgear maker support the T&D equipment capex cycle and the premium valuations for electrical-equipment companies.

industrials.headline: Green Energy Corridor-III: ₹1.86 trillion plan for intra-state renewable transmission
industrials.summary: The Centre has launched the third phase of the Green Energy Corridor scheme, with a total project outlay of ₹1.86 trillion and central financial assistance of ₹54,082 crore, 83% of it for transmission. The scheme targets evacuation of 135 GW of renewable capacity and 50 GWh of battery storage, and private transmission companies can bid under tariff-based competitive bidding. Officials expect ₹8–9 trillion of investment under GEC through 2035.
industrials.whyItMatters: A large, centrally supported intra-state tendering pipeline adds to order visibility for transmission EPC, conductor, transformer and BESS suppliers, and to the asset base available to InvITs and private transmission platforms.

industrials.headline: Zetwerk lists 5.5% above issue price after ₹5,012 crore IPO subscribed 3.06x
industrials.summary: Contract manufacturer Zetwerk listed at ₹159.25 on the NSE, 5.46% above its ₹151 issue price, and at ₹159 on the BSE. The ₹5,012 crore IPO, comprising a ₹2,830 crore fresh issue and a ₹2,182 crore offer for sale, was subscribed 3.06 times, with QIBs at 4.73x and retail at 0.73x. About ₹2,160 crore of the fresh proceeds will repay debt; FY26 revenue was ₹15,913 crore.
industrials.whyItMatters: A modest debut after lukewarm retail demand shows investors are pricing new-age manufacturing platforms selectively, a useful read for the pipeline of industrial and contract-manufacturing IPOs.

aerospace-defence.headline: Tonbo Imaging lists at a 66% premium after a 136x subscribed IPO
aerospace-defence.summary: Defence electro-optics maker Tonbo Imaging listed at ₹1,162 on the BSE and ₹1,160 on the NSE, about 66% above its ₹700 issue price, implying a market value of ₹6,656 crore at the BSE listing price. The ₹852 crore IPO was entirely an offer for sale of about 1.22 crore shares, so the company received no proceeds, and was subscribed 135.9 times. Anchor investors had taken ₹255.4 crore.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: A strong debut for a private defence-tech company supports valuations for the pipeline of defence and electronics IPOs and gives existing PE and VC holders a clear exit route.

aerospace-defence.headline: Solar Defence's Nagastra-2 loitering munition clears trials and is delivered to the Army
aerospace-defence.summary: Nagpur-based Solar Defence & Aerospace said its Nagastra-2 loitering munition completed technical trials at the Mahajan field firing range in August and has been delivered to the Indian Army. The system carries a 4 kg tandem shaped-charge warhead, has a range of 25 km in recoverable mode and 50 km in fire-and-forget mode, and up to 60 minutes of endurance. Quantity and order value were not disclosed.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Repeat loitering-munition inductions from a private supplier show the Army's growing reliance on domestic drone makers, a theme drawing PE interest and possible consolidation in the unmanned-systems space.

regulatory.headline: MoRTH proposes mandatory emergency braking on new car models from October 2030
regulatory.summary: MoRTH has issued a draft amendment to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules that would make Advanced Emergency Braking Systems mandatory on newly launched M1 passenger-vehicle models from 1 October 2030 and on all M1 models from 1 October 2032. The draft also proposes AEBS for new truck and bus models from January 2027, ESC and a revised braking standard for trucks from October 2027, and V2V communication on all new vehicles from October 2028. The draft is open for 30 days of public consultation.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Mandated ADAS content raises per-vehicle electronics and sensor spend, supporting radar, camera and braking suppliers and potentially prompting technology tie-ups and acquisitions by Indian component makers.

regulatory.headline: India's October flash composite PMI rises to a four-month high of 56.7; input cost inflation eases
regulatory.summary: The HSBC flash composite PMI rose to 56.7 in October from 55.9, as services rose to 56.2 from 55.2, while manufacturing eased to 54.9 from 55.1. Input-cost inflation slowed for a seventh straight month to its lowest in nearly a year, although firms cited higher steel and transport costs, and factory-gate price increases were the softest in almost four years.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Easing input-cost inflation could help margins at capital-goods and auto companies in H2, though weak pricing power suggests limited room to pass on costs.

regulatory.headline: G-sec yields rise for a tenth straight week, the longest streak in three decades
regulatory.summary: The benchmark 10-year government bond yield closed at 7.47%, up about 10 bps over the week and marking a tenth consecutive weekly rise. Traders cited Brent crude reaching a five-month high near $116 a barrel after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, along with higher US yields.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Rising sovereign yields increase benchmark borrowing costs for corporate bonds and infrastructure debt, affecting the pricing and timing of DCM issuance by capital-goods, power and auto-finance issuers.
